simple.meaning: מאוּם (mʼûwm) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a blemish (physically or morally).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 22 times across Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 2 Samuel, Job, and 3 more, beginning at Leviticus 21:17. Its contexts include flock, offering, sacrifice, altar, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מאוּם (H3971).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מאוּם (mʼûwm) / H3971 is traced through Leviticus 21:17, Leviticus 21:18, Leviticus 21:21, Leviticus 21:23 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: “Say to Aaron, ‘None of your offspring throughout their generations who has a defect may approach to offer the bread of his God.
For whatever man he is that has a defect, he shall not draw near: a blind man, or a lame, or he who has a flat nose, or any deformity,

No man of the offspring of Aaron the priest who has a defect shall come near to offer the offerings of Yahweh made by fire. Since he has a defect, he shall not come near to offer the bread of his God.

No man of the offspring of Aaron the priest who has a defect shall come near to offer the offerings of Yahweh made by fire. Since he has a defect, he shall not come near to offer the bread of his God.
He shall not come near to the veil, nor come near to the altar, because he has a defect; that he may not profane my sanctuaries, for I am Yahweh who sanctifies them.’ ”
But you shall not offer whatever has a defect, for it shall not be acceptable for you.
Whoever offers a sacrifice of peace offerings to Yahweh to accomplish a vow, or for a free will offering of the herd or of the flock, it shall be perfect to be accepted. It shall have no defect.
You must not offer any of these as the bread of your God from the hand of a foreigner, because their corruption is in them. There is a defect in them. They shall not be accepted for you.’ ”
If anyone injures his neighbor, it shall be done to him as he has done:
fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. It shall be done to him as he has injured someone.
“This is the statute of the law which Yahweh has commanded. Tell the children of Israel to bring you a red heifer without spot, in which is no defect, and which was never yoked.
If it has any defect—is lame or blind, or has any defect whatever, you shall not sacrifice it to Yahweh your God.
If it has any defect—is lame or blind, or has any defect whatever, you shall not sacrifice it to Yahweh your God.
You shall not sacrifice to Yahweh your God an ox or a sheep in which is a defect or anything evil; for that is an abomination to Yahweh your God.
They have dealt corruptly with him.
Now in all Israel there was no one to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty. From the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no defect in him.
Surely then you will lift up your face without spot;
if my step has turned out of the way,
One who corrects a mocker invites insult.

definitions.full: H3971. mum מאוּם noun masculine Job 31:7 blemish, defect (for מְאוּם , which, although found only late, is (si vera lectio) apparently original form, .Kö ii. 146 ); — ׳מ absolute: 1 of physical defect Dan 1:4 . 2 figurative מ דָּבַק ׳בְּכַמַּי Job 31:7 of moral stain; usually מוּם noun masculine Lev 21:17 (= foregoing; quiescent א omitted) (Late Hebrew id. ; Aramaic מוּמָא , ); — absolute ׳מ 21:17 16 t.; suffix מוּמוֺ Prov 9:7 ; מוּמָם Deut 32:5 ; — blemish, defect (chiefly H): 1 physical , a. in man, as excluding from priestly service , Lev 21:17-18 , 21 (twice in verse); 21:23 ; disfiguring man 2Sam 14:25 , woman Song 4:7 ; (in all מ ׳היה בְּ ); as caused by man upon man Lev 24:19-20 ,. b. in beast (reference to sacrifice) Lev 22:20-21 , 25 ; Num 19:2 ; Deut 15:21 (twice in verse); 17:1 (in all מ ׳היה בְּ ). 2 figurative of moral blemish Deut 32:5 (but text very dubious, compare Dr); מִמּוּם פָנֶיךָ תִּשָּׂא Job 11:15 ; of shame of repulse Prov 9:7 ׅ || (קָלוֺן .
definitions.rootNote: usually מוּם ; as if passive participle from an unused root probably meaning to stain
